source: WHO AFRO Zoonotic Disease Protocols, WHO Expert Consultation on Rabies 2018, OIE One Health Framework

exposure_types.bite: Direct bite - break in skin; highest rabies transmission risk
exposure_types.scratch: Scratch or abrasion from claws/teeth - moderate risk
exposure_types.contact: Mucous membrane or broken skin contact with saliva/body fluids
exposure_types.consumption: Consumption of raw/undercooked meat or unpasteurised dairy
exposure_types.vector_borne: Tick, flea, or fly bite in context of animal contact

risk_factors: animal ill or died after bite
rabies.management: Immediate wound wash (soap + water 15 min), rabies PEP (see rabies_pep_protocol), rabies immunoglobulin (RIG) for Category III exposures

brucellosis.treatment: Doxycycline 100mg BD x 6 weeks + Rifampicin 600mg OD x 6 weeks (or Doxycycline + Streptomycin IM for severe/neurobrucellosis)
brucellosis.note: Most common zoonosis in SADC pastoral communities. Check cattle/goat vaccination status. Notifiable.

rift_valley_fever.treatment: Supportive. Ribavirin may reduce severity if started early (specialist decision). Barrier nursing. Notifiable - outbreak trigger.
rift_valley_fever.note: Epidemic-prone. Aedes and Culex mosquitoes amplify. Notify national surveillance immediately.

forms.cutaneous: Painless black eschar - 95% of cases; treat with Amoxicillin 500mg TDS x 7 days or Ciprofloxacin 500mg BD x 7 days
forms.gastrointestinal: Nausea, vomiting, bloody diarrhoea after consuming infected meat - high mortality; IV Ciprofloxacin + Metronidazole
forms.inhalational: Rare; near 100% mortality without treatment; medical emergency

anthrax.treatment: Ciprofloxacin 500mg BD x 7-60 days OR Doxycycline 100mg BD. Add anthrax antitoxin in severe cases (if available).
anthrax.note: Handle carcasses with PPE. Notifiable. Do NOT perform post-mortem on suspected anthrax animals - releases spores.

leptospirosis.treatment: Mild: Doxycycline 100mg BD x 7 days. Severe (Weil's disease): IV Penicillin G 1.5MU Q6H or IV Ceftriaxone 1g OD x 7 days.
leptospirosis.note: Exposure via flood water, rice paddies, livestock urine. Rodent control key prevention.

q_fever.treatment: Acute: Doxycycline 100mg BD x 14-21 days. Chronic Q fever/endocarditis: Doxycycline + Hydroxychloroquine x 18 months (specialist).
q_fever.note: Coxiella burnetii survives in dry environments for months. Parturient animals high risk.

human_african_trypanosomiasis.treatment: Stage 1: Pentamidine (T. b. gambiense) or Suramin (T. b. rhodesiense). Stage 2: Eflornithine (gambiense) or Melarsoprol (rhodesiense). Specialist only.
human_african_trypanosomiasis.note: Notifiable. Report to national HAT control programme. WHO supports free treatment in endemic areas.

wound_categories.I: Touching/feeding animal, licks on intact skin - no PEP required
wound_categories.II: Nibbling/minor scratches without bleeding - wound wash + vaccine only
wound_categories.III: Single/multiple transdermal bites, scratches with bleeding, licks on broken skin, mucous membrane contact - wound wash + vaccine + RIG

essen_protocol.vaccine: Rabies vaccine (cell-culture derived: HDCV, PCECV, or PVRV)
essen_protocol.note: Day 0 = day of exposure/presentation. All 5 doses must be completed.

zagreb_protocol.note: 2 doses on day 0 (different sites), then day 7 and 21. WHO-accepted alternative.

rig_dosing.route: Infiltrate as much as possible into wound, remainder IM at distant site from vaccine
rig_dosing.timing: Same day as first vaccine dose (day 0) - never after day 7

high_risk_combinations.action: IMMEDIATE wound wash + Category assessment + Start PEP day 0
Treat as Category III regardless - bats have minor bites not always noticed
Serology + stool culture if febrile. Doxycycline + Rifampicin if confirmed.
PCR + serology if febrile within 6 days. Notify surveillance if suspected.
Doxycycline prophylaxis if high-risk flood exposure. Serology if symptomatic.
